samples.identity: Sality v4 infection of a PyInstaller command-line downloader
evidence: PyInstaller cookie at file offset 0x642d7c describes Python 3.7 CArchive starting at 0x4cc00. Extracted downloader_req.pyc was disassembled using xdis: sys.argv supplies URL and destination, requests.get(timeout=10) obtains bytes, and open(filepath, wb).write stores them. No implicit launch or fixed remote endpoint appears in that Python program.

Entry 0x407a6a instead runs polymorphic arithmetic, calls/pops a code pointer into EBX, transfers it through MM5 to EBP, computes a return target, and returns to 0x44d899 in executable/writable .reloc. Local Unicorn emulation performed no host API calls and reconstructed the native code in memory.

A multi-round arithmetic decoder reaches the recovered native entry at 0x44e916; it walks the PEB and export directory to resolve APIs. At 0x44f148 it validates an embedded MZ/PE, allocates executable memory, copies sections, applies fixups, and resolves imports for an embedded DLL.

Embedded UPX DLL at memory VA 0x451e02, size 0xb400, unpacked successfully with UPX. The unpacked body contains the existing Sality v4 RSA public-key fingerprint, IPFILTERDRIVER and kukutrustnet rendezvous hosts. This establishes family identity independently of the filename and vendor labels.

Unpacked DLL entry 0x434567 starts multiple worker threads and calls initialization at 0x433b60. Initialization opens SharedAccess FirewallPolicy StandardProfile and passes a zero REG_DWORD to RegSetValueExA for EnableFirewall at 0x433eac; the next writes clear DoNotAllowExceptions and set DisableNotifications.

Unpacked function 0x42e329 maps executable files and reconstructs/rewrites their PE content, adjusts file size, writes modified data at 0x43084c, and restores timestamps. Function 0x431ef6 allocates remote memory, writes a code buffer at 0x432382 and passes the same allocation to CreateRemoteThread at 0x4323b0.
samples.judgment_context: The grafted native infector is unrelated to the downloader purpose. No deployment assumption is needed to judge the modified executable malicious; the original downloader alone is dual-use.
samples.coverage_limit: Two hostile outer-file traits cover the concealed native decoder and its Sality identity. The 3-5 goal is unmet: infection, remote-thread injection, firewall impairment and mapped-DLL activation are recoverable only after the custom arithmetic decoder followed by UPX. cleave facts exposes no decoded DLL layer for that native transform. The full archive scan, manual emulation, UPX extraction, extracted-stage scan and instruction-level traces were attempted. Ciphertext, generic imports, or inherited runtime DLL capabilities were not promoted into unsupported outer-file claims. Engine decoding or a proven ciphertext-independent behavioral signature is required for those additional behaviors.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Original and revised ML levels remain -1 despite two supported hostile traits; probability rises from 0.713621 to 0.91773844. No inaccurate rule was introduced to force a threshold.

evidence: Selects a writable executable staging directory by writing/chmodding/executing a no-op probe; probes are removed. Enumerates /proc/*/comm to avoid launching a second miner.
Tries two HTTP base URLs and wget, curl, then inline Python urllib. Retrieves bin/xmrig, falls back to bin/xmrig-static, chmods and executes --version.

Selects a Plex Media Server Cache directory, copies the miner under PlexMediaScanner, and runs it detached with an external config and CPU thread hint. The source explicitly calls this killer bypass. This concealment tips the judgment beyond ordinary user-managed XMRig.
Chooses light/full config according to RAM, requires an author-selected wallet prefix while rejecting another, sets a host-derived worker identifier, and selects ceil(0.85 * CPU cores) threads.

Writes hidden agent/watchdog scripts. The agent restores a deleted cache binary from the persistent backup; a PID-guarded watchdog invokes it every 45 seconds. Installs an every-minute crontab entry to the hidden agent. The agent skips execution when one of its miner aliases is already running.
samples.judgment_context: Invocation, authorization and the remote configuration contents are absent. The combination of an unrelated application identity/cache, bypass commentary, fixed payout validation and durable covert relaunch supports malicious resource abuse.
samples.coverage: Three hostile traits cover concealment, concealed mining deployment and cron reactivation. Neutral staging, detached configured launch, dotfile script writing and scheduled-script facts were added. A shared cp matcher was broadened to handle whitespace and then cp; no previous matcher population was narrowed.
samples.classifier_disagreement: ML moves from below the calibrated grid (level -1, probability 0.95210564) to level 25 / confidence 92 with three hostile traits (reported probability 0.98).

evidence: Byte-for-byte identical to BusyBox 1.36.1 shell/ash_test/ash-misc/shift.tests fetched through forager with provenance retained in scratch.

If given no arguments, reexecutes itself via the harness THIS_SH with fixed test arguments. Echoes positional arguments and tests ordinary, excessive and repeated shifts. There are no URLs, dependencies, encoded stages, persistence changes or payload execution beyond its own interpreter test.
samples.source_label_explanation: No malicious behavior is present. Its external acquisition/deployment context was not supplied; a broad shell-execution heuristic or association with a larger collected artifact could explain the source label, but that provenance is unconfirmed.
samples.coverage: Preserved the accurate variable-command exec trait and added a neutral positional-shift observation. No benign suppressor was added. Hostile/suspicious counts remain zero; ML stays below grid.

regression_evidence.copy_matcher: All 14 preexisting matches found in textual testdata at most 1 MB were retained, including hostile shell/JS/keychain and PAM chain fixtures outside this batch. Consumers of exact cp IDs and ancestor selectors were inspected; no severity reduction or rule removal occurred.
regression_evidence.controls: Ordinary explicit miner install, Plex cache maintenance, hidden backup cron, cp commands, cp prose, BusyBox shift test, extracted downloader bytecode, existing native benign PE and local credential-backup fixtures do not fire the new hostile traits. A miner copy with changed IPs, script/config names, payload aliases and wallet prefixes retains all three new hostile detections.
regression_evidence.old_sality_coverage: The existing MMX/ECX and relocation-branch rules and both consumers are untouched. The new EBP instruction shape was absent from those required signatures; the additions are independent alternatives and do not replace original coverage.
regression_evidence.losses: No finding IDs or severities were lost across any original sample or scanned archive member. All 171 emitted Windows artifact/member records were compared.
regression_evidence.warning: Atomscan reports that model v18 feature specifications lag the current v21 schema; final validation is run separately and must have no warnings.
